title: Petra and the Wolf
premise: Petra Jonah Whitlock, an exiled storm-caller hiding under a false name in the magic-free city of Greyhollow, discovers the old gods are answering prayers again because something has broken beneath Mount Cael: the Undercourt's thirteenth moon-cycle seal. The wolf that shadows her turns out to be her brother Aldric, whose soul was sold to the court twelve years ago by their mother to buy Petra's exile instead of her execution. To free him, Petra must steal his soul back from the Court Beneath the Mountain before the moon completes its thirteenth turn, but reclaiming it means surrendering her own storm-gift as payment. In the end she outwits the court by splitting the debt across every descendant of the original bargain, freeing Aldric at the cost of her power, and the two siblings walk out of the mountain mortal, memory-broken, and finally free.
about_author: Lena Ravensworth is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing folk charms in northern mining towns before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about inheritance, debt, and the things families refuse to say aloud.

chapters.title: Charms for the Godless
chapters.summary: Petra sells a luck-knot to a grieving widow in Greyhollow, where magic is outlawed, and feels the first tremor of returning storm-power in her scarred hands. Her POV establishes her fear of her own gift and the quiet loneliness of exile. Emotional beat: guarded hope curdling into dread when the charm actually works.

chapters.title: The Prayer That Answered Back
chapters.summary: A stranger's desperate prayer in the market square is audibly answered by something old, and the city's Wardens begin arresting anyone with 'god-touched' marks. Petra recognizes the answering voice as one from her childhood. Her POV; beat: terror of exposure mixed with an ache of homesickness for magic.

chapters.title: The Wolf at the Threshold
chapters.summary: A grey wolf begins following Petra home each night, unafraid, watching her with unsettlingly human eyes. She dreams of a frozen lake and a boy drowning beneath it. Her POV; beat: creeping recognition that the animal knows her name.

chapters.title: Warden Vess
chapters.summary: Warden Ilse Vess, hunting god-touched fugitives, corners Petra and offers immunity in exchange for informing on other practitioners. Petra lies well enough to survive the meeting but is now marked. Vess's POV chapter reveals her own dead daughter and her hatred of gods who answer too late. Beat: mutual, wary respect.

chapters.title: What Mother Sold
chapters.summary: Petra finds her mother's old ledger hidden in a smuggler's cache: a contract selling 'one soul, the elder child' to the Court Beneath the Mountain, signed twelve years ago. Her POV; beat: devastation reframed as purpose — the wolf must be Aldric.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: An astronomer-priest confirms the moon will complete its thirteenth turn in twenty-eight days, when the Undercourt's seal opens and all debts come due. Petra realizes her deadline. Her POV interwoven with Aldric-the-wolf's fragmentary memories. Beat: the clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Road
chapters.summary: Petra buys passage with a charm-smuggling caravan toward Mount Cael, forced to use small magics that risk everything. The wolf travels openly beside her, unnerving the caravaners. Her POV; beat: exhilaration of using her gift again, shadowed by guilt over those she endangers.

chapters.title: Village of Answered Prayers
chapters.summary: The caravan passes a village where every prayer has been granted grotesquely literally — rain that never stops, a harvest of teeth. Petra understands the gods' return is not mercy but malfunction. Her POV; beat: horror at what unchecked divine power does to ordinary people.

chapters.title: Warden's Bargain
chapters.summary: Vess catches up to the caravan, having traced Petra, but a god-touched mob attacks before she can arrest her; Petra saves Vess's life with a storm-call that levels a hillside. Vess's POV; beat: her certainty cracks — she owes a witch her life.

chapters.title: The Wolf Speaks
chapters.summary: At a mountain shrine, the seal's proximity lets Aldric hold human shape for one hour. Brother and sister speak for the first time in twelve years; he remembers being sold, and forgives her — which is worse than blame. Alternating POV; beat: grief and tenderness, love complicated by guilt.

chapters.title: The Gate of Teeth
chapters.summary: They reach the sealed gate beneath the mountain as the moon nears fullness, guarded by the Hollow Priest, who demands a toll of memory for passage. Petra pays a memory of her mother's face. Her POV; beat: sacrifice as strategy, loss as currency.

chapters.title: Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Inside, the Undercourt is a cathedral of frozen petitioners — everyone whose prayers were answered and never released. Petra sees the machinery of divine power: prayers harvested like ore. Her POV; beat: awe curdling into righteous anger.

chapters.title: The Queen of Quiet Things
chapters.summary: The Undercourt's queen explains the bargain: souls bought keep the gods asleep; the seal breaking means the gods wake hungry. She offers Petra Aldric's soul in exchange for Petra's storm-gift, freely given. Her POV; beat: temptation — a fair trade, almost.

chapters.title: Ledger of Debts
chapters.summary: Petra stalls, requesting to audit the original contract, and discovers her mother didn't sell only Aldric — she pledged the whole bloodline as collateral. The queen's claim on Petra is legal and eternal. Her POV; beat: despair deepening into cold clarity.

chapters.title: What Vess Carried Down
chapters.summary: Vess arrives, having followed, carrying her daughter's unanswered prayer-letter. In the court's presence the letter finally receives its answer — twelve years late. Vess's POV; beat: rage at divine indifference becomes her willingness to help Petra break the system itself.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn Begins
chapters.summary: The moon completes its turn; the seal cracks; the sleeping gods stir, and the frozen petitioners begin to scream awake. Chaos erupts in the court. Multiple POV; beat: catastrophe as opportunity — the rules are breaking.

chapters.title: Storm-Caller's Choice
chapters.summary: With the court collapsing, Petra must choose: take the offered trade and save only Aldric, or gamble on rewriting the contract mid-catastrophe. She chooses the gamble, invoking the bloodline clause. Her POV; beat: courage as refusal of the terms given.

chapters.title: The Debt Divided
chapters.summary: Petra argues before the waking queen that a pledge made by one mother binds all descendants equally — and names every living Whitlock kin, spreading the debt so thin no single soul can be claimed. The court's own law traps it. Her POV; beat: triumph through cleverness, the theme of inheritance weaponized.

chapters.title: Aldric Unbound
chapters.summary: Aldric's soul is released; the price is Petra's storm-gift, torn out in a scene of terrible beauty as the mountain shakes. He carries her toward the gate as the court floods with freed petitioners. Alternating POV; beat: bittersweet liberation — freedom purchased with identity.

chapters.title: The Gods Wake Hungry
chapters.summary: Escaping the collapsing mountain, they pass the newly woken gods rising like weather systems over the world — no longer bound, no longer fed. Vess stays behind to negotiate, or die trying. Vess's POV; beat: sacrifice and unresolved stakes, the world changed forever.

chapters.title: Greyhollow After Rain
chapters.summary: Petra and Aldric return to Greyhollow, powerless and anonymous, and reopen the charm stall — now selling honest trinkets. The city's magic ban is meaningless; the gods are loose, but small human luck still matters. Her POV; beat: quiet peace, ordinary life reclaimed.

chapters.title: Petra and the Wolf
chapters.summary: On the first night of true winter, Aldric chooses to remain a wolf sometimes, and Petra finds she sleeps better with him at the door. A final image: two siblings, memory-scarred and mortal, watching the thirteenth moon set. Shared POV; beat: acceptance — inheritance is not destiny, and family is what survives.
